newsitem.title: CHINA: China says no frost damage to wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: China says no frost damage to wheat crop.

text.p: Chinese officials said on Tuesday frost had not affected wheat crops in the northeast or in eastern and central provinces.

"Wheat in our region has not been influenced by frost because we plant spring wheat," an official of the meteorological bureau in the northeastern wheat-growing province of Heilongjiang said by telephone.
"Winter wheat can be affected by frost, but winter wheat accounts for a very small part of the total," he said.
Officials in central Henan, another large wheat-producing province, said the crop had not been affected by frost and there had been plenty of rain since March but warned of pest damage.
"The overcast and rainy weather is bringing pests and diseases due to lack of sunshine," a local meteorological official said.
"The pest and disease could affect wheat growth, but we are now taking preventative measures," he said.
An official in eastern Shandong province said the weather had been favourable for the wheat crop.
"Compared with last year, the climate for wheat is relatively good and no frost has occurred," the meteorological official said.
